messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'dp-tritondynamics-01' high GPU utilization detected. GPUs 0-3 at 97-100% for 2m, request queue length 230, avg wait 12s. paging @oncall-sre.
Alex: I’m on it — looking at queue metrics now. tagging @jamal and @mira.
Mira: seeing lots of long-running generation jobs pinned to gpt-large-quant; top_k=200 on some requests. trace id 0x9f3e in logs.
Jamal: dp-tritondynamics-01 is single-tenant reserved pool, autoscale policy is set to "reserved-only" — burst is currently disabled per contract. Do we have exec approval to temporarily allow burst?
Sophie: pinged CS to confirm contract. TritonDynamics contacted us last month about extra bursts being possible with add-on. they’re on a platinum plan but didn't purchase burst credits. I’m messaging their infra lead now.
Alex: while we wait, short-term mitigations: 1) throttle non-prod jobs from the tenant, 2) route inference requests over 1k tokens to hosted fallback model (rdw-infra/hosted-gpt-medium), 3) consider burst override for 10 minutes. can someone run the routing override?
Mira: I can flip a routing rule. propose: reroute requests with header X-Cust-Tier: noncritical to fallback, and set max_tokens cap 1024 on pool ingress.
Jamal: to enable burst override I need ops approval + audit note. If we do burst, GPUs will come from shared spare capacity and could impact other Dedicated customers slightly.
Alex: call with SRE lead — @nate can you authorize a one-time 15-min burst override if CS gets customer approval? we need clear rollback.
Nate: I can approve a 15-min, provided we: 1) set hard timeout 15m, 2) enable auto-fallback to hosted after 10m if avg latency > 3s, 3) capture audit event.
Sophie: Triton responded: "we're seeing production degradation, please do whatever is needed; we'll reconcile billing later." they gave verbal OK. sending written confirm now.
incident-bot: Note: audit window created id=aw-4732, hold-until 2026-03-15T18:05:00Z.
Jamal: ok enabling burst_override for dp-tritondynamics-01 for 15m now. running command:
```
rdwctl pools burst-override --pool dp-tritondynamics-01 --duration 900 --reason "customer outage - verbal approval" --audit-id aw-4732
```
Jamal: executed. cluster reports +2 GPUs provisioned from spare-capacity pool. queue length dropping to 48.
Mira: pushed routing rule to push noncritical to hosted fallback:
```
ruleset add route --pool dp-tritondynamics-01 --match "X-TD-Stage!=prod" --to hosted-gpt-medium
```
requests per-second down ~35%.
Alex: monitoring logs — 500s error rate for large-context jobs dropped from 4.2% -> 0.6%. latency tail improved. still seeing some heavy long tokens.
Sophie: TritonCS says application saw immediate relief, thanks. They want continuous updates and a postmortem.
Nate: set automatic rollback at +15m and set canary fallback policy if latency spikes after rollback.
Jamal: scheduling eviction of best-effort redispatchables: kicking non-prod tenants queued on same server to different nodes. command: `rdwctl evict --pool dp-tritondynamics-01 --label best-effort --dry-run=false`
Alex: executed eviction, freed ~6% GPU load. queue now 9.
Mira: I also applied a temporary model-variant config to reduce top_k on large streams: patched config to clamp top_k<=50 for requests >2000 tokens.
Alex: good. putting "incident: tri-dp-gpu-exhaustion" on incident board. tagging in followup checklist: postmortem owner, billing reconciliation, contract review for burst credits.
incident-bot: Reminder: on-call handoff in 25m. next oncall is @olivia.
Olivia: ack, I'm standing by for handoff. please summarise state when you hand off.
Alex: current state: burst_override active, expires in ~6m; queue=9, avg wait 1.2s, latency p95=1.9s. TritonCS confirmed they see normal traffic. Next steps: watch rollback at expiry, prepare to re-enable routing if rollback causes queueing.
Sophie: I'll schedule an immediate sync with Triton for 30m to explain mitigations and collect logs.
Nate: assign postmortem to Mira, include timeline, root cause (single tenant burst of long-context requests + conservative autoscale policy), and recommendations: enable burst credits, add transfer plan for enterprise pools, consider predictive autoscale threshold for sustained queue>100.
Mira: taking postmortem. will collect traces and produce impact metrics (affected requests, minutes of elevated latency, mitigations applied).
Alex: thanks all. handing off to @olivia in 2m. final note: no cross-tenant SLA breaches flagged; monitor shared spare capacity usage.
Olivia: thanks @alex — I have ops console and will watch the rollback. ping if anything changes. :eyes:
